title: Pam the Cat
learning_objectives: Decode CVC words with short a
Read the sight words the, a, is, in, on by sight
parent_prompts: Point under each word. Let the child sound out c-a-t, b-a-g, n-a-p before you say anything.
If the child guesses from the picture, cover the picture and try the word again.
After reading: Where did Pam nap? Was that a good place?

pages.text: Sam has a cat. The cat is Pam.
pages.illustration_brief: Sam sitting on a mat; a grey cat beside Sam. Do not show a bag yet.
pages.audio_script: Sam has a cat. The cat is Pam.
pages.image_alt: Sam sitting on a striped mat with a grey cat beside.

pages.text: Sam has a bag. The bag is on the mat.
pages.illustration_brief: A blue school bag lying open on a striped mat; Sam packing a book into it.
pages.audio_script: Sam has a bag. The bag is on the mat.
pages.image_alt: A blue school bag lying open on the mat; Sam packing a book.

pages.illustration_brief: Only the cat's tail and one ear stick out of the bag; Sam is looking the other way.
pages.image_alt: Only a cat tail and one ear stick out of the bag; Sam looks away.

pages.text: Sam taps the bag. Pat, pat.
pages.illustration_brief: Sam's hand on the bag, puzzled face; a bulge in the bag.
pages.audio_script: Sam taps the bag. Pat, pat.
pages.image_alt: Sam's hand on the bag, puzzled face; a bulge in the bag.

pages.text: Pam! No nap in my bag!
pages.illustration_brief: Pam's head pops out of the bag, eyes wide; Sam laughing.
pages.audio_script: Pam! No nap in my bag!
pages.image_alt: The cat's head pops out of the bag, eyes wide; Sam laughing.

pages.text: Pam naps on the mat. Sam has the bag.
pages.illustration_brief: Pam curled on the mat asleep; Sam walking away with the bag on one shoulder.
pages.audio_script: Pam naps on the mat. Sam has the bag.
pages.image_alt: The cat curled asleep on the mat; Sam walking away with the bag on one shoulder.

quiz.explanation: n-a-p. It starts with n and ends with p.
Page 3 says: Pam naps in the bag.

quiz.prompt: Why does Sam tap the bag?
quiz.explanation: Pam napped in the bag (page 3), so the bag looked strange and Sam tapped it (page 4).

quiz.prompt: Tell a grown-up where Pam napped first and where Pam napped at the end.
quiz.rubric: not yet: points at the cat only; with support: names one place with prompting; independent: says in the bag, then on the mat, and why Sam moved her
quiz.explanation: Naming both places shows the child tracked the change, not just the picture.

activities.prompt: Match the word to its meaning.

pairs.right: a small rug on the floor

off_screen_prompt: Find three things at home whose names have the a sound like cat. Say them to someone.

review.decodability_note: Pam, Sam, cat, bag, mat, nap(s), tap(s), pat are short-a CVC; 'naps'/'taps' carry an -s ending, accepted after review. All other words are on the irregular list.
